The absence of occupational history is a gap — but does not negate the diagnosis, as exposure may be remote, unrecognized, or secondary (e.g., family member’s occupation, living near mining/construction sites).

[EVIDENCE]  
- Bilateral interstitial fibrosis with reticulonodular opacities on HRCT  
- Eggshell calcification of multiple mediastinal/hilar lymph nodes  
- Reduced FEV1/FVC ratio  
- Reduced DLCO  
- Isolated exertional dyspnea for 1 year without systemic symptoms  
- No smoking history, no cardiac/pulmonary comorbidities  
- No orthopnea, PND, edema, cough, wheeze, chest pain, or fatigue  

[GAPS]  
- Occupational and environmental exposure history (e.g., sandblasting, mining, stone cutting, foundry work, concrete mixing)  
- Duration and intensity of any potential silica exposure  
- Serum anti-silica antibodies (not clinically used, but research context)  
- BAL fluid analysis (e.g., silica-laden macrophages — though rarely seen in chronic silicosis due to fibrotic sequestration)  
- Surgical lung biopsy showing birefringent silica particles (gold standard but rarely performed)  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Chronic silicosis
